verdict: Compliance fanouts (RBI purpose code, FIRC, LUT, GST on export of services, SOFTEX) are the largest fanout family in the focus set, and skydo.com wins almost none of them: the 17 compliance URLs that get fetched at all total 72 fetches and 30 citations. ChatGPT cites government pages first and then short, signed, code-specific guides. Skydo's purpose-code blog is 4,044 words with 103 bullets and 30 H3s and was cited zero times in nine fetches; the FIRC guide is 6,418 words and was cited zero times in six.

a.chat: How to receive International Payments in India as a Architecture Firms (winvesta cited 6 times)
a.answer: Use the correct RBI purpose code: P1009 – Architectural, Engineering and Other Technical Services. Include this purpose code on your invoice. LUT if exporting services without charging IGST. Keep FIRA, invoice, contract, payment advice.
a.page: H3 What P1009 covers; H3 How to use P1009 when invoicing; H3 GST; H3 Workflow

a.chat: Freelancer tax fanouts (livemint cited 2.2 per fetch)
a.answer: Presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA up to ₹50 lakh (₹75 lakh if 95% digital); report under Income from Business or Profession, ITR-4 or ITR-3; advance tax if liability exceeds ₹10,000; LUT to export without IGST; keep FIRC/e-FIRA and Form 67.

diagnosis: Compliance fanouts are answered with a rule, a number and a source. Government pages win because they are the source; guides win when they carry section numbers, form names, thresholds and dates.

One page per code or form. ChatGPT cites the page about P1009, the page about LUT, the page about reporting overseas income. Skydo's all-codes page and all-about-FIRC page are never the best source for any single fanout.
Question headings match fanout phrasing. Livemint's five H2 questions are the questions ChatGPT was asked to answer.
A copyable line beats an explanation: the invoice line 'RBI Purpose Code: P1009 — Architectural, Engineering and Other Technical Services' was reproduced verbatim.
A 2025 date on a rules page loses to a 2026 date. Rules pages need a visible 'updated' date and a 'what changed in 2026' line.
Product sections between rules cost citations. 'How Skydo automates FIRC' inside a FIRC explainer signals a sales page; the crawler also broke Skydo's table headers.

Skydo's short single-topic pages (p0807, importance-of-fira, softex) already cite at 0.8 to 2.0 per fetch. The bucket needs more of those and fewer 6,000-word guides. This is the consolidation project on the Consolidation Plan tab.
spec: One reference page per entity: each purpose code Skydo supports (P0802, P0807, P0805, P1009, P1006...), FIRC, FIRA, e-FIRC, LUT, SOFTEX, EDF, eBRC, EDPMS, GST on export of services, Section 44ADA, realisation window.

Each page 700-1,500 words: definition in the first sentence; who it applies to; the neighbour term and how to choose; the exact line to put on the invoice or form; the government path (portal menu, form number); the dates and thresholds; what happens if wrong; a 5-step workflow; FAQ of 4-6.
Named author with credential (CA or the compliance lead), visible published and updated dates, 'what changed in 2026' line, Article + FAQPage schema.
Cite the RBI/CBIC/DGFT source by circular number with an outbound link on every page.
No product section in the body. One line at the end: 'Skydo tags this code automatically and issues a FIRA on every payment.'
Redirect the long guides into the new pages or trim them to hub pages that link out.

playbook.bucket: Compliance reference: purpose codes, FIRC/FIRA, LUT, SOFTEX, FEMA
playbook.use_when: The fanout asks for a rule: 'RBI purpose code for software exports', 'FIRC vs FIRA', 'LUT for export of services', 'GST on foreign client income', 'SOFTEX form'. ChatGPT answers with the rule, the number or form, and cites the source.
blueprint: One page per code, form or rule. Title is the entity plus the year: 'P0802 purpose code (2026): software consultancy exports'.
First sentence is the definition. Second is who it applies to.
Neighbour section: the code or form it is confused with and the rule for choosing.
Copyable line: the exact text for the invoice, the form field, or the portal menu path with the form number.
Numbers and dates: thresholds, windows, fees, the circular number, 'what changed in 2026'.
What happens if you get it wrong, in three sentences.
FAQ of 4-6 questions phrased the way the fanouts are phrased.
700-1,500 words. Named author with credential, published and updated dates, outbound link to the RBI/CBIC/DGFT source, Article + FAQPage schema.
No product section in the body. One closing line on how Skydo handles it. One CTA.
